description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:45-49 and 118; src/backend.rs:12 and 14-17.

```rust
// lib.rs
pub use backend::{
    AddedItem, BackendChangesError, BackendSetError, ChangesResult, FileNodeBackend, GetObject,
    JmapBackend, JmapObject, QueryChangesResult, QueryObject, QueryResult, SetError, SetErrorType,
    SetObject,
};
...
pub use jmap_filenode_types::JMAP_FILENODE_URI;
...
pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;

// backend.rs
pub use jmap_filenode_types::backend::FileNodeProperty;
...
pub use jmap_server::{
    AddedItem, BackendChangesError, BackendSetError, ChangesResult, GetObject, JmapBackend,
    JmapObject, QueryChangesResult, QueryObject, QueryResult, SetError, SetErrorType, SetObject,
};
```

Fifteen upstream types are re-exported from this crate's public surface.
Every one binds the upstream major version: if `jmap-server` cuts a
SemVer-major to change e.g. `BackendSetError`, `jmap-filenode-server`'s
own public surface breaks at the same boundary even if no FileNode
behaviour changed.

Two questions for the maintainer:

1. **Are all of these actually used by consumers?** A consumer that
   implements `FileNodeBackend` needs `JmapBackend`, `SetError`,
   `SetErrorType`, `BackendSetError`, `BackendChangesError`,
   `ChangesResult`, `QueryResult`, `QueryChangesResult`. They probably
   also need `JmapObject`, `GetObject`, `QueryObject`, `SetObject`
   as trait bounds. They do NOT need `AddedItem` — it is a wrapper
   used internally by `QueryChangesResult`. They do NOT need
   `ClosureHandler` — it is the concrete handler type that
   `register_filenode_handlers` constructs internally. They do NOT
   need `FileNodeProperty` — it is only referenced by the trait but
   not by handler code.

2. **Should the re-exports go through `jmap_filenode_server::types`
   or similar namespace?** Top-level re-exports collide with the
   crate's own types and force consumers to disambiguate. A
   sub-module re-export (`jmap_filenode_server::backend::JmapBackend`)
   keeps the namespacing explicit and signals "this is an upstream
   convenience".

The lib.rs:118 `pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler` is particularly
suspect — it is the concrete type built by the `reg!` macro inside
`register_filenode_handlers`. No external consumer should need to
name it. Either `#[doc(hidden)]` it or remove the re-export.

Same propagation pattern across siblings (the canonical
jmap-mail-server has the same kind of top-level re-export shape).
Apply the fix to mail-server first per the canonical-template rule,
then propagate.

This is `api-contract,versioning` because every re-export increases
the public-surface area that must be maintained across upstream
revisions. Trim what consumers do not need; keep what they do.
title: Re-exports of upstream types lock jmap-server's major version into this crate's public surface
